The print comes amid mounting scrutiny over MARA’s strategic pivot from a pure-play Bitcoin
miner to an artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure provider.

Earlier this year, the firm moved away from its long-standing Bitcoin holding strategy and began selling its reserves to raise cash and reduce debt. It has sold more than 18K Bitcoin since March. Its Bitcoin holdings fell from 53.8K BTC at the end of 2025 to 35.6K BTC by the end of the second quarter, reducing its Bitcoin holdings per share by about 34%.

reached about $59.8K per Bitcoin. Its adjusted EBITDA showed an $18M loss, excluding changes in Bitcoin's market value.
Although the company had 70.3 EH/s of mining capacity, higher network difficulty and energy costs continued to weigh on its business.

However, Wall Street analysts remain cautious, along with Seeking Alpha analysts having a Hold rating on the stock, with a score of 3.00, while the Quant rating stands at Strong Sell, at 1.26, reflecting concerns about profitability and growth.

Investors will focus on three main catalysts on Monday: progress on securing a first signed AI tenant, updated Bitcoin monetization details, and the impact of Bitcoin's price changes on its third-quarter earnings.
